title: {{NAME}} and the Royal Paleontology Expedition
moral: The best discoveries come to those who combine curiosity with careful preparation.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a dusty tan expedition jacket, dark adventure trousers, and heavy excavation boots — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
Princess Veda had been waiting three years to excavate the Stonegrey Quarry.

Every survey had indicated significant fossil deposits beneath the old mine. Every previous expedition had been turned back by the unstable terrain.

{{NAME}} had built DELVE: an excavation robot with stabilisation arrays and the ability to map underground space in three dimensions before putting a tool to the rock.

"You've solved the stability problem," said the princess, reviewing his design.

"DELVE goes in first," said {{NAME}}. "Maps everything. We work with the map."

"When do we leave?" she said.

pages.content:
DELVE's first map of the Stonegrey Quarry revealed: extraordinary fossil deposits across four strata, the largest concentration either {{NAME}} or the princess had ever seen.

Also: a large cavity in the middle of the main deposit that DELVE identified as a nest chamber.

"That's a communal nest," said Princess Veda, barely breathing. "Multiple species. We've never found one this intact."

"DELVE says it's stable if we approach from the north quadrant," said {{NAME}}. "And if we take our time."

pages.content:
The excavation took four days.

DELVE cleared rock. The princess identified and documented. {{NAME}} maintained DELVE and managed the site safety.

On day two: the nest chamber. Intact eggs, fossilised, a hundred million years of stillness.

On day three: the skull of an adult Parasaurolophus, positioned at the nest entrance.

"It was guarding the nest," said Princess Veda. She was speaking very quietly.

"Still is," said {{NAME}}.

pages.content:
The finds were catalogued over the last day: twenty-three fossilised eggs, two adult specimens, and nest structure that would rewrite the current understanding of Parasaurolophus social behaviour.

Princess Veda wrote the initial report in the field tent that evening, DELVE's data filling the gaps her observations left.

"I've done eight expeditions," she said. "None of them like this."

"DELVE had the map right," said {{NAME}}.

"You built DELVE right," she said. "That's what it comes down to."

pages.content:
He fell asleep in the field tent that night with the fossils catalogued and the report nearly done.

He thought about the Parasaurolophus at the nest entrance: a hundred million years of waiting, just to be found and understood.

DELVE hummed softly, running overnight diagnostics.

The quarry was quiet above them.

He closed his eyes and thought: there is so much still in the ground. So many things waiting to be known.

He slept, and dreamed of walking through time.
